jobs.title: Cribl: Sr. UX Designer, Security
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote
URL: https://cribl.io/

Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You’ll Love This Role

We are looking for a Senior Product Designer to help define and deliver Cribl security product experience. You will design for security practitioners across detection, alerting, investigation, triage, search, threat coverage, telemetry, and AI-assisted workflows.

This role requires a genuine security background and the ability to turn complex SOC workflows into clear, trustworthy experiences. You will partner with Product, Engineering, UX Research, and other designers to create a cohesive experience that works seamlessly with our other products across the entire Cribl platform.


As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

  • Lead end-to-end design from problem framing and research through interaction design, prototyping, validation, and implementation.
  • Design workflows for detection creation and management, alert review, investigation, triage, search pivots, threat coverage, normalization, and enrichment.
  • Apply security judgment to evidence, provenance, confidence, severity, permissions, auditability, destructive actions, and operational risk.
  • Design AI-assisted and agentic experiences that make intent, context, sources, capabilities, uncertainty, and user approval clear.
  • Use Cribl’s design system and contribute reusable components, patterns, guidance, and interaction models when the work has broader value.
  • Work expertly in Figma for exploration, prototyping, documentation, collaboration, and handoff, including libraries, variables, components, variants, and tokens.
  • Partner with engineers, PMs and designers through ideation, development to support feasibility, accessibility, resilience, and high-fidelity implementation challenges.
  • Share work early and often through critiques and working sessions. Give and receive specific, constructive feedback.
  • Use research and product evidence to prioritize opportunities, evaluate concepts, and improve shipped workflows.
  • Communicate design rationale, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical partners.
  • We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones - you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours.


If You’ve Got It - We Want It

  • Required:
    • 5+ years experience designing complex B2B software, enterprise platforms, or products for technical users.
    • A security background, such as security product design, security operations, threat detection, incident response, threat hunting, detection engineering, SOC workflows, SIEM, EDR, SOAR, or a related discipline.
    • Understanding of security practitioners’ realities, including noisy signals, incomplete evidence, time pressure, and high-consequence decisions.
    • Strong product thinking and interaction-design skills, with the ability to make complex technical workflows simple without oversimplifying them.
    • Experience designing AI-assisted, agentic, conversational, or other emerging interaction models.
    • Expert Figma skills, including advanced prototyping and design documentation.
    • Demonstrated expertise working in and contributing to design systems. You know when to use existing patterns and when to extend them thoughtfully.
    • Understanding of AI tools and AI UX interaction models is required. You can design experiences where AI assists, recommends, generates, investigates, or takes action while preserving user understanding, control, and trust.
    • Experience collaborating closely with Product and Engineering in an iterative and changing environment.
    • Strong communication, facilitation, and problem solving skills, including the ability to make progress when information is incomplete.
    • A portfolio with case studies that show your role, process, decisions, collaboration, and outcomes. Candidates will be asked to present and discuss previous work.
  • Highly desired:
    • Familiarity with research tools such as Dovetail, including transcripts, tagging, themes, repositories, and insights.
    • Experience with security data, detections, alerts, investigations, threat intelligence, telemetry, data pipelines, or analytical workflows.
    • Experience designing for roles, permissions, tenants, environments, or different levels of technical expertise.
  • A plus
    • Understanding of accessible product design and inclusive interaction practices.
    • Familiarity with WCAG principles, keyboard interactions, focus management, semantic structure, color contrast, and accessible content patterns.
    • Familiarity with OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK, KQL, Sigma, detection rules, threat intelligence, or related concepts.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/cribl-sr-ux-designer-security

Art Direction & Retail Assets

  • Design retail displays, point-of-sale materials, and supporting brand assets.
  • Keep retail-facing assets aligned with the live packaging system.

Collaboration & Stakeholder Presentation

  • Work with marketing, product development, production, and external vendors on each launch.
  • Present concepts and design rationale to internal stakeholders and clients.
  • Manage feedback cycles and turn revisions around within project timelines.

Creative Leadership

  • Mentor junior designers on packaging and production standards.
  • Review team output against brand and print-quality standards.
  • Document design standards and file conventions for reuse across projects.


Requirements

Must-Have

  • Experience designing for consumer electronics, wellness, lifestyle, or consumer packaged goods brands
  • Demonstrated development of brand identities extended across packaging, retail, and marketing touchpoints

Nice-to-Have

  • Figma for brand systems and cross-functional collaboration

jobs.title: Hightouch: Deployment Architect
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote (North America)

About Hightouch

Hightouch is an Agentic Marketing Platform powered by the industry-leading Composable CDP. With complete brand context, customer data, and performance history in one place, every marketer finally has the power to build and ship end-to-end campaigns themselves. Teams move faster, stay on brand, and get AI marketing that actually works.

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Francisco, Hightouch enables marketing teams to analyze performance, brainstorm ideas, and generate creative at a speed and quality that wasn't previously possible.

Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Customer Data Platforms, Hightouch is trusted by leading enterprises like Domino's, Spotify, Aritzia, Cars.com, Ramp, and PetSmart.

At Hightouch, our mission is to help our customers leverage data and AI to grow their businesses. The team is ambitious, impact-driven, efficient — and we believe humility, kindness, and compassion are essential to our success. If you're energized by velocity, obsessed with raising the bar, and want to build alongside people who care deeply about each other and our customers, we'd love to meet you.

About The Role 

As an Deployment Architect, you will be the force behind successful deployments at Hightouch. Working in close partnership with an account team and the Hightouch product team, you will own the full deployment and enablement lifecycle for Hightouch customers. You will be the primary point of contact for customers during deployment and are responsible for executing the technical aspects of customer onboarding, ensuring seamless integration of Hightouch into customers' existing data infrastructure.

In this role, you will be the product expert who translates complex customer requirements into actionable implementation plans. You should have a natural ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to both data engineering teams and business stakeholders. As the primary owner of the deployment lifecycle, your focus is on creating repeatable, efficient implementation processes that scale across our customer base while maintaining the flexibility to address unique enterprise needs.

What You’ll Do

  • Drive the onboarding process for customers, working closely with the Account team to ensure alignment between technical execution and customer success objectives
  • Design and optimize deployment frameworks that can scale across different customer segments while accommodating enterprise-specific requirements
  • Lead technical discovery sessions and implementation workshops, collaborating with customer data engineering teams and business stakeholders
  • Create and maintain detailed technical documentation for deployments, including integration specifications, data models, and best practices
  • Develop and execute implementation plans that minimize time-to-value while ensuring robust, sustainable solutions
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to identify and resolve technical blockers that could impact customer success
  • Build relationships with technical stakeholders within customer organizations
  • Contribute to product development by providing feedback to our engineering team
  • Standardize and automate implementation processes to increase team efficiency and customer satisfaction

What We're Looking For

  • 5-10 years of experience in technical implementation, solutions architecture, or similar roles with enterprise software
  • Strong technical background with hands-on experience in data integration, APIs, and enterprise architecture
  • Proven track record of successfully managing complex technical implementations while maintaining clear communication with a variety of stakeholders
  • The ability to tackle the most ambiguous customer problems (the "that can't be done" ones) and find a creative paths to successful implementation
  • Experience creating and optimizing implementation processes that can scale across an organization
  • Excellence in technical project management with ability to manage multiple concurrent implementations
  • Strong presentation and facilitation skills with ability to command a room of technical and business audiences
  • Experience working with data warehouses, ETL processes, and marketing technology is a plus
  • Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience)

The salary range for this position is $140,000-$180,000 USD per year, which is location independent in accordance with our remote-first policy. We also offer meaningful equity compensation.

E-Verify Statement

Hightouch participates in E-Verify. After you join the team, we'll verify your eligibility to work in the U.S. by submitting information from your Form I-9 to the Social Security Administration and, if needed, the Department of Homeland Security. This process happens post-hire only — we never use E-Verify to pre-screen applicants.

jobs.title: Squarespace: Senior Staff Operations Manager, Office of the President (PED)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, California

We are looking for a Chief of Staff–style operator to serve as the President’s right hand and help run, maintain, and continuously evolve the Product, Engineering & Design operating model and cadence. 

This role will turn strategy into a durable execution system. You will own the connective tissue across the President’s leadership cadence: preparing the right inputs, creating clarity on decisions and tradeoffs, ensuring commitments are followed through, surfacing risks early, and improving the operating model as the organization changes. You will work across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Finance, People, and your peers in Business Operations, partnering with senior leaders who do not report to you and influencing through judgment, trust, and clarity.

The successful candidate will combine executive judgment, operational rigor, business acumen, comfort with ambiguity, strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to move fluidly between strategic questions and the execution details required to make the system work. 

AI fluency is an important part of this role. You will use approved enterprise AI tools, including tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable platforms, to automate repeatable operating work, synthesize information across functions, improve leadership preparation, surface risks and dependencies, and accelerate strategic-initiative delivery.

This role reports to the VP of Operations at Squarespace and is based remotely in California or locally at our New York City headquarters. 

You’ll Get To… 

  • Run the President's operating cadence. Own end-to-end orchestration of the leadership rhythm: staff meetings, WBRs, MBRs, and QBRs, finance and portfolio reviews, priority updates, and annual operating-plan inputs. Ensure each ritual has a clear purpose, owner, input, output, decision authority, and downstream cascade.
  • Drive decision quality. Synthesize diverse inputs into concise narratives that make priorities, risks, options, tradeoffs, and recommended decisions clear to the President and leadership team. Document decisions in the room, assign owners and deadlines, track commitments, and escalate unresolved issues with context and a proposed path forward.
  • Improve execution velocity. Identify alignment and execution risks before they surface as leadership surprises, and facilitate resolution across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Customer Operations, Finance, People, and Business Operations, connecting planning, performance, financial, organizational, and roadmap inputs. Use AI and advanced tooling to make decisions faster and better-informed.
  • Evolve the operating model. Treat the operating system as a living thing. Establish health measures such as decision latency, action closure, cascade reach, pre-read quality, participation, recurring issue themes, and use them to assess whether rituals, artifacts, and escalation paths are producing the right outcomes. Recommend and implement changes to cadence, governance, templates, roles, and channels as strategy and priorities evolve, codifying what works so the model is easy for leaders to understand and operate.
  • Lead high-priority strategic initiatives. Drive complex, ambiguous, cross-functional work on behalf of the President, from framing and workplan through decision, implementation, and follow-through, including emerging problems that don't yet have a clear owner. Support annual strategy, goals, headcount, and budget processes by connecting them to the department's operating rhythm.
  • Represent the President and build transparency. Stand in for the President in meetings, events, and discussions, exercising the remit of the position. Navigate difficult conversations and cross-functional tradeoffs without relying on formal authority. Support two-way access to the President through Town Halls, Roundtables, Office Hours, and written follow-up, using sound judgment about what should be broadly communicated, selectively shared, or handled privately.
  • Serve as a trusted thought partner to the President and senior leadership team, offering an independent perspective and respectfully challenging assumptions when needed.

Who We’re Looking For

  • Significant experience in Chief of Staff, Product Operations, Business Operations, Strategy & Operations, or management consulting
  • A track record of owning an operating model, leadership cadence, or portfolio of complex cross-functional initiatives, preferably in tech companies
  • Knowledge of the product / software development lifecycle
  • Demonstrated proficiency with enterprise AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable approved tools, and experience integrating them into daily workflows to automate repeatable tasks, optimize processes, improve synthesis, and accelerate project delivery.
  • Exceptional written communication: you can turn a large volume of input into a concise, decision-ready narrative tailored to the audience
  • Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand metrics, forecasts, resource tradeoffs, product or portfolio performance, and organizational implications.
  • Strong executive presence and facilitation skills; you can create clarity and momentum in high-stakes or ambiguous settings.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, build consensus, resolve conflict, and push for decisions without formal authority.
  • High judgment and discretion when handling sensitive organizational, people, financial, and strategic information.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, switching between strategic altitude and detailed execution, and taking ownership of problems that cross organizational boundaries.
  • A continuous-improvement mindset: you distinguish between process and content, challenge ineffective routines, and make change practical and durable.
  • A bias toward action, paired with the judgment to know when to decide, when to seek input, and when to escalate.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 6–12 months, you will:

  • Implement a dependable operating rhythm in which leadership forums are well-prepared, decision-oriented, and followed through.
  • Improve the quality and consistency of pre-reads, decision logs, action tracking, portfolio updates, and quarterly communications.
  • Make it easy to see what changed, what matters now, what decisions are needed, who owns the next step, and where risk is accumulating.
  • Establish a small number of reliable AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual preparation and reporting effort, improve the timeliness and quality of leadership inputs, and make follow-through more visible.
  • Increase the organization’s ability to reuse knowledge, detect recurring issues, and move from raw information to clear decisions without adding unnecessary process.
  • Build strong working relationships and trust with the President and his leaders across the department and company, leading with tact, discretion and respect.
  • Help the President and leadership team make faster, clearer, better-informed decisions without adding unnecessary processes or meetings.
  • Leave the system more scalable and more resilient than you found it.

Benefits & Perks

  • A choice between medical plans with an option for 100% covered premiums including medical, dental, and vision
  • Supplemental Life and Disability Insurance plans
  • Fertility and adoption benefits
  • Headspace mindfulness app subscription
  • Global Employee Assistance Program
  • Retirement benefits with employer match
  • Flexible paid time off
  • 12 weeks paid parental leave and family care leave
  • Pretax commuter benefit
  • Education reimbursement
  • Employee donation match to community organizations
  • 7 Global Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)
  • Dog-friendly workplace
  • Free lunch and snacks
  • Private rooftop
  • Hack week twice per year

US Cash Compensation Range: $178,500 - $350,000 USD

The base salary for this position will vary based on job-related criteria including relevant skills, experience, and location, among other factors.

In addition to the cash compensation above (which includes base salary and, where applicable for eligible roles, may include overtime pay), Squarespace employees are eligible to be granted an option to purchase our common stock. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive structure in addition to base salary.

About Squarespace

Squarespace is a design-driven platform helping entrepreneurs build brands and businesses online. Description

SaaS Revenue & Financial Analyst — Flosum

About Flosum

Flosum is a Salesforce-native platform company delivering enterprise-grade DevOps, data protection, and security solutions to some of the world's largest organizations. Our product portfolio spans Cloud DevOps, Data Migrator, Data Masking, Data Backup, Org Security, Cloud Trust Center, and Sandbox Synchronization — all built natively on the Salesforce platform. We serve enterprise customers across technology, energy, financial services, healthcare, and federal government. Flosum is a growth-stage company operating with the intensity and speed of a startup backed by the discipline of a mature operator.

The Role

We're hiring a SaaS Revenue & Financial Analyst who will own the measurement layer of our entire business. You will be the person who knows every number — ARR, net retention, expansion, churn, pipeline conversion, cost of acquisition, gross margin by product line, services margin, cash flow, and everything in between. You'll work across Salesforce (our CRM and billing system of record) and QuickBooks (our financial system) to build a unified, always-current picture of company performance.

This is not a reporting role. This is an analytical role where you connect revenue operations data to financial outcomes and surface the insights that drive decisions at the CEO level.

What You'll Own

You will build and maintain our SaaS metrics infrastructure — ARR waterfall, cohort retention analysis, revenue recognition schedules, deferred revenue tracking, and unit economics by segment. You will reconcile Salesforce bookings data against QuickBooks revenue entries and ensure we have a single source of truth across both systems. You will produce monthly and quarterly financial and revenue packages for leadership, including variance analysis against plan. You will model scenarios for pricing changes, product bundling, geographic expansion, and headcount investment. You will monitor pipeline health and translate pipeline data into revenue forecasts with documented assumptions. You will own the data integrity between our CRM and accounting systems, flagging discrepancies before they compound. You will support board-level and investor-level reporting with clean, defensible metrics.



Requirements

What We're Looking For

You have three-plus years of experience in SaaS financial analysis, revenue operations, or FP&A at a B2B software company. You are deeply proficient in Salesforce — not as a user, but as someone who understands opportunity objects, product schedules, contract structures, and reporting at a data level. You are equally proficient in QuickBooks Online, including chart of accounts design, revenue categorization, journal entries, and reconciliation workflows. You understand ASC 606 revenue recognition principles and can apply them to a multi-product SaaS business with annual and multi-year contracts. You can build financial models from scratch in Excel or Google Sheets — not from templates, from logic. You think in terms of cohorts, not just totals. You understand the difference between bookings, billings, and revenue, and you can explain why each matters. You are precise, skeptical of your own numbers, and obsessive about data integrity.

Preferred

Experience at a company with a mix of subscription revenue and professional services. Familiarity with Salesforce CPQ or native Salesforce quoting and contract objects. Exposure to investor or board reporting at a growth-stage company. Experience with Marketo or HubSpot data as it relates to CAC and attribution modeling.

Why Flosum

You'll report directly into the CEO's operating rhythm. Your work will not sit in a queue — it will shape hiring plans, product investment, and go-to-market strategy in real time. Flosum is building the definitive platform for Salesforce lifecycle management, and we need someone who can measure every dimension of that growth with precision.

jobs.title: ZoomInfo Technologies LLC: Principal Infrastructure Architect: Data Platform
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen–fast.

 

As a Principal Infrastructure Architect on our Infrastructure Architecture team, you will be the architecture team's partner to ZoomInfo's data engineering organization. Data engineering owns the platforms and the products built on them. You bring the infrastructure patterns, evaluation rigor, and cross-team alignment that help them build and run those platforms well on GCP.

This is a cloud architect seat with a data specialty. You bring the same cloud, Kubernetes, networking, and infrastructure-as-code foundation as the rest of the architecture team, plus enough hands-on depth in data systems to be credible with the engineers who run them.

The work breaks down four ways:

  • Patterns. You establish and maintain the paved-road patterns data teams build on: infrastructure as code, CI/CD for data jobs and pipelines, monitoring and alerting, performance, and cost. You keep them easy to consume and self-service.
  • Enablement and alignment. You help data teams adopt those patterns, review their designs, and work through hard infrastructure trade-offs with them.
  • Evaluation. You run POCs of new data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process, and you write recommendations engineering leaders can act on.
  • Shared stewardship. You take a full share of the architecture team's general work: weekly architecture reviews across all domains, standards and ADRs, and infrastructure consulting for any team that needs it.

The data estate is broad. We don't expect deep experience across all of it. We expect real depth in some areas and the ability to build depth in others as the work demands. Patterns get adopted here through leadership and communication rather than positional authority. You'll write reference implementations, open the first PRs, and stay hands-on through enablement when a critical initiative calls for it.

What You'll Do

  • Establish infrastructure patterns for data workloads. Design and maintain reference patterns for provisioning and operating the data platforms ZoomInfo runs: streaming and messaging (Kafka/Confluent, Pub/Sub), operational databases (PostgreSQL/Cloud SQL, MongoDB), analytical stores (BigQuery, Snowflake), search (Elasticsearch/Solr), pipeline orchestration and processing (Apache Airflow/Cloud Composer, Dataflow/Apache Beam), and open table formats (Apache Iceberg). Ship them as Terraform modules, GitOps workflows, and documented standards that data teams can adopt without reinventing them.
  • Build the data paved road. Today's delivery tooling is application-centric. Define CI/CD and GitOps patterns for data jobs and pipelines, and partner with platform engineering and data engineering to make data delivery as safe and automated as application delivery.
  • Establish performance, cost, and observability patterns. Give data teams the patterns and guidance to run stores and pipelines efficiently (query and storage optimization, partitioning and clustering, tiering and retention, workload isolation, right-sizing) and the monitoring, alerting, and SLO practices that make performance and cost visible. Set the baseline patterns for backup, restore, and disaster recovery of data stores, including RTO/RPO targets. Partner with FinOps on data-layer spend. Review workloads with teams against these patterns and help them align.
  • Evaluate new technologies. Run structured POCs of emerging data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process. Recent examples include graph and distributed SQL databases, stream processing (Apache Flink, Confluent Flink), and schema management and cataloging. Weigh self-hosted against vendor-managed, map migration and exit paths, model cost, and write up a recommendation.
  • Bring managed data services inside the perimeter. Define the patterns for connecting vendor-managed data planes (Confluent Cloud, Snowflake, MongoDB Atlas, and similar) to our GCP environment: private connectivity (Private Service Connect, PrivateLink, VPC peering), VPC Service Controls, identity and encryption across the boundary (workload identity, CMEK, in-transit), and the DNS and routing that go with them. Model egress and cross-region cost, and set the exfiltration controls that keep those services inside the compliance perimeter.
  • Support data consolidation and governance efforts. Contribute infrastructure guidance to data engineering's work on consolidating where data lives and is accessed (BigQuery, Snowflake, object storage) and on data classification, residency, and access policy.
  • Prototype and hand off. Build the reference implementation, write the ADR, and partner with the owning teams to roll the pattern out. Stay hands-on through POC and initial enablement.
  • Participate in architecture review. Bring a consistent, documented rubric to weekly architecture reviews across all domains, including designs that have nothing to do with data. Expand the standards library and ADR catalog. Take a share of the team's general consulting and support load.
  • Enable teams. Host design reviews and workshops. Serve as the infrastructure consultant to data teams making complex choices.

What We're Looking For

  • Influence and communication. You can present a recommendation, show its value, and back it with prototypes, benchmarks, and documented rationale. You've gotten patterns adopted across engineering organizations you don't manage by working with the teams involved.
  • Cloud infrastructure foundation. Production experience architecting on GCP and/or AWS beyond the data services: compute and Kubernetes (GKE or equivalent) as the runtime for data workloads, VPC networking and private connectivity to managed services, IAM and workload identity, and cost and reliability trade-offs. Strong Terraform and GitOps skills, including designing and reviewing modules other teams depend on. You can review a service-mesh or network design in architecture review with credibility.
  • Hands-on data infrastructure experience at scale. You've built and operated the infrastructure under data platforms at multi-terabyte to petabyte scale, with high throughput, high concurrency, and latency-sensitive workloads, and you know what breaks in production.
  • Depth in at least two data domains, fluency across the rest. Deep production experience in at least two of: streaming and stream processing (Kafka/Confluent, Flink); relational operational databases (PostgreSQL); NoSQL (MongoDB); columnar analytics and lakehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, Iceberg); search (Elasticsearch/Solr); pipeline orchestration and processing (Airflow, Dataflow/Beam). Enough fluency in the others to evaluate, review, and learn them quickly.
  • Performance and cost engineering. You've diagnosed and fixed expensive or slow data workloads (query plans, storage layout, pipeline design, warehouse spend) and turned the fixes into reusable patterns and monitoring that other teams picked up.
  • Development and operational depth. You can dive into code to prove out a pattern and test behavior under load, and you'd rather ship a working prototype than a diagram.
  • Technology evaluation. You've run rigorous evaluations that separate vendor pitch from architectural fit, and your recommendations have been used by engineering leaders and procurement.

Bonus Points

  • Supported a lakehouse or data mesh migration from the infrastructure side.
  • Implemented data classification, residency, or privacy/compliance (GDPR/CCPA) controls at the infrastructure layer.
  • Run graph or distributed SQL databases in production.
  • Know the infrastructure demands of AI/ML data workloads (feature stores, vector databases, embedding pipelines).
  • Built or applied AI-augmented developer or architecture workflows (agent-driven pipeline provisioning, MCP servers, LLM-based rubric evaluation).
  • Run or participated in an Architecture Review Council or equivalent governance body.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10–15+ years of cloud infrastructure, platform, or data infrastructure engineering experience, including several years establishing patterns and standards that multiple teams depend on.

Are you a driven back-end developer who doesn't wait for instructions, but is already thinking two steps ahead? Who experiments with new technologies and smart solutions alongside the job? Then we want to talk to you.

Straight forward but clear: Twikey isn't looking for someone to just execute. We're looking for someone who thinks, does and keeps going when the going gets tough.

Because fintech is evolving at breakneck speed. That calls for real ownership and for someone who can dive deep on the technical side to keep innovating and improving our platform. You get plenty in return, such as the freedom and responsibility to deliver your own projects. Thanks in part to our organisational structure, you can shape your ideas in the short term and see the results of your hard work quickly.

Driven by your passion for building scalable, performant and secure back-end systems, you continuously raise the bar for your own skills and for our product.

As a member of our development team you work closely with our CTO, 3 fellow developers and 2 testers on the core of our software application. A small, strong team in which you take on a role with real impact on the future of our product.

  • You focus on developing and improving the back-end of our platform, optimising the architecture and data processing while keeping the security and stability of our system in mind. This lets you put your technical skills to full use and come up with innovative solutions.
  • With your expertise you'll make valuable suggestions and streamline processes for all our stakeholders, so we can work more efficiently and achieve better results.
  • You provide technical support on integration projects with software houses, banks and large companies, solving complex technical problems. That gives you the chance to work on challenging projects and to get in touch with a wide range of technologies and industries.

Once you know our product inside out, there are plenty of challenging projects for you to help build.

What are we looking for in you?

  • You are driven, curious and enterprising. Not only in your job, but outside of it too. You have a pro-active attitude and are always a few steps ahead: you spot opportunities, grab them and get to work.
  • Technical challenges? You take them on, not because you have to, but because you want to learn. You're a self-starter and quickly get to grips with new technologies, languages or frameworks.
  • You understand that a good product is never "finished". You draw energy from that mix of creating and fine-tuning. You think along, question things and keep building new solutions.
  • You have experience using AI tools to build integrations. You're actively exploring how AI can contribute to smarter user experiences and more efficient software development. Experience with data analytics is an asset.
  • You therefore attach a lot of importance to the security, stability and reliability of a system and know what it takes to get there. You work in a structured, meticulous way and write code that is clean, reusable and easy to test.
  • You have demonstrable experience with Java, Go and the Spring framework. Experience with API integrations, web services, Linux or other relevant areas is a plus.
  • You have a deep understanding of databases. You don't just know how to use them, you know how they work. You have an opinion on structured, high-quality code, architecture and back-end technologies.
  • You have a very good command of English, for smooth collaboration with all colleagues and stakeholders. Dutch is an asset.
  • You are based in a time zone within one hour of CET, so your working day overlaps with the team's for the daily stand-ups and close day-to-day collaboration.
  • You can work independently and enjoy a small team where switching gears quickly, collaboration and knowledge sharing are central.

Twikey offers you:

  • An environment where challenge, innovation and autonomy come first.
  • The room to experiment, to challenge and to improve. And we expect you to really take that room.
  • An ideal setting if you want to grow fast and healthily, both technically and personally. Training, ownership, taking on new or additional roles based on your talents and interests, ... a lot is possible here, and you're at the wheel!
  • A complementary team of more than 35 colleagues who move forward together in a respectful and open atmosphere.
  • A motivating workplace with plenty of knowledge and expertise, shared both formally during the daily stand-ups and the weekly Friday call, and informally at the coffee machine.
  • Appreciation, openness and critical dialogue. Our Friction Hunter Trophy is an example: every month we celebrate the colleague who made the biggest difference for customers, teammates or internally. Your impact gets noticed!
  • A modern workplace with different zones (conference, connect, co-work, concentrate) in a recently built, industrial-style office building. Easy to reach by car, by bike and by public transport on the edge of Ghent, right next to the KBC tower.
  • A salary package tailored to your experience and skills, with plenty of extra-legal benefits, a collective bonus system and a cafeteria plan to convert your 13th month as you choose.
  • The chance to work in an innovative Belgian fintech scale-up that is active in several countries, in a sector that is growing fast!

A job ad doesn't tell you everything. Our colleagues tell you here what it's really like to work at Twikey.

Commercial Data Scientist

Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients. 

At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.


This role can be filled in the Northeast (New York, NJ, Philadelphia, Boston), our San Francisco headquarters, OR other remote locations in the U.S.

As a Commercial Data Scientist, you’ll work within cross-functional delivery teams alongside other analysts, engineers, and commercial stakeholders in discovering data insights to help improve healthcare.

How you’ll make an impact:

  • Deliver novel and impactful insights for client organizations using machine learning and AI technologies.
  • Work closely with our Product, Platform Data, Insights & Strategy, and Sales teams to create client-facing analyses.
  • Showcase your engineering skills by creating data products from scratch and automating code so they can be re-used by other teammates and future projects.
  • Leverage Doximity's extensive datasets to identify and classify behavioral patterns of medical professionals on our platform.
  • Embrace the challenge of a fast-paced environment to exceed client expectations

 

The Core Values of the Client Intelligence team

As an organization we value diversity - in backgrounds and in experiences. Healthcare is a universal concern, and we need people from all backgrounds to help build a better future for all. Below are additional core values specific to the Insights Team.

  • Collaboration—The best candidates and teammates are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.
  • Passion for Data—You’re going to help our clients and team members with data-driven decision making. We need someone that can manipulate millions of rows of data and also ask the right questions to find the important insights.
  • Reliability – Our team is efficient, flexible, and agile only because we trust the reliability of each member. We need self-starters and goal-oriented individuals for our continued success.
  • Curiosity – Continuous learning is a cornerstone at Doximity, and curious individuals thrive in our environment. We’re looking for someone who is curious enough about data to go above-and-beyond the task for the true insight.
  • Respect – A key dynamic that allows our team to flourish is respect: for ourselves and our quality of work, for our teammates, and for our internal clients who are under the pressure of deadlines and finance goals.

 

About you:

  • At least 4 years of professional experience as a Data Scientist or other related roles working with complex, high-volume, structured and unstructured datasets.
  • Prior experience in a data science consulting role at firms such as ZS, Trinity, IQVIA, BlueMatter, etc., where you thrived in a fast-paced environment
  • Advanced knowledge of statistical concepts — particularly exploratory data analysis, experimental design, and probability theory.
  • Deep understanding of modern machine learning techniques
  • Proven ability to design, train, and evaluate large-scale production models using frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
  • Advanced SQL proficiency — skilled at writing and optimizing complex queries across multiple tables and data relationships.
  • Advanced Python skills, including understanding of object-oriented programming, production-grade code design, and modern data science libraries.
  • Hands-on experience with distributed data processing tools and concepts for scalable analysis and model training.
  • Excellent data visualization and storytelling abilities, with the capacity to translate technical insights into clear, compelling narratives for internal and client stakeholders.
  • Curious, fast learner with a demonstrated passion for data, continuous learning, and staying current with advances in machine learning research.

 

Fun Facts About the Client Intelligence team

  • We have access to one of the richest healthcare datasets in the world, with deep information on hundreds of thousands of clinicians and their connections.
  • Business decisions at Doximity are driven by our data, analyses, and insights.
  • The members of our team bring a diverse set of technical and cultural backgrounds.
  • We like to have fun - company outings, team lunches, and other social events!

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

  • Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.

jobs.title: Vercel: Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - United States

About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About the Role:

AI Gateway gives developers one place to connect applications and agents to hundreds of models with one API key. It handles provider routing and fallbacks, unifies billing and observability, and lets teams manage spend and security controls across production AI workloads.

Designing this well is a systems problem. A developer should be able to choose the right model, make and verify a first request, diagnose a failed request, and configure routing, budgets, credentials, and security controls without losing sight of the application they are trying to build. The right interface might be in the dashboard, on the public model catalog, in the CLI, in an API response, or in code.

You will be the Design Engineer for AI Gateway, owning product design and frontend implementation across those surfaces. You will work with customers, a Product Manager, and engineers to understand the problem, explore solutions, build the production experience, ship it, and learn from what happens after launch.

AI Gateway is live, the model ecosystem changes every week, and the team can move from an observed problem to production quickly. This is a rare chance to use your product judgment, design craft, and code to shape a developer product and ship the experience yourself.

You will be the design owner embedded with a Product Manager and a dedicated engineering team. You will also have the Product Design team around you for critique, collaboration, and support. AI Gateway will be your main product area, with room to pursue design-led improvements across Vercel. You will report to the Design Team.

If you’re based within a pre-determined commuting distance of one of our offices (SF, NY, London, or Berlin), the role includes in-office anchor days on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday. If you're located beyond that distance, the role is fully remote. For location-specific details, please connect with our recruiting team.

What You Will Do:

  • Own product design and frontend implementation for meaningful parts of the journey from discovering a model to making a first successful request and operating AI in production.
  • Design and build production experiences across the website, dashboard, CLI, and APIs, choosing the right medium for each problem.
  • Make models, providers, credentials, routing, budgets, logs, performance, privacy, and governance understandable, then create patterns that extend across new providers, modalities, and workloads.
  • Talk directly with customers and use product data to understand problems, define success, make tradeoffs, and improve what ships.
  • Own quality after launch, including visual and interaction craft, accessibility, performance, resilience, instrumentation, and edge cases.
  • Use coding agents to explore and implement ideas quickly, while testing, debugging, and taking responsibility for what ships.

About You:

  • Your work shows what you personally identified, designed, built, shipped, and learned after launch.
  • You build production-quality web applications with React and TypeScript and can contribute confidently in a large, existing codebase.
  • You bring strong visual and interaction craft and have made technical or data-rich products understandable without removing the control advanced users need.
  • You can move between graphical interfaces, CLI workflows, API behavior, and implementation details, treating accessibility, performance, failure recovery, and instrumentation as part of the design.
  • You use customer research and product data to make decisions, communicate your reasoning clearly, challenge ideas constructively, and change direction when the evidence changes.
  • You use coding agents in your daily work, but you can explain, test, debug, and take responsibility for the code they help produce.

There is no required path into this role. You may come from product design, frontend engineering, creative development, or a career that does not fit a standard title. We care about the quality of what you have shipped and the judgment behind it.

jobs.title: Calm.com: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, United States

About Calm

Calm is the leading mental health brand on a mission to make the world happier and healthier. Known for its flagship consumer app—ranked #1 in its category with over 180 million downloads and availability in ten languages across 190 countries—Calm helps people sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully through content and tools from experts and beloved celebrity voices. Building on this foundation, Calm has created a broader portfolio including evidence-based solutions like Calm Health, offered through employers, health plans and providers, designed to expand access to mental health and sleep support, boost benefits engagement, and drive positive health outcomes. Today, Calm supports more than 3,500 organizations and reaches over 42 million covered lives through Calm Health. Calm has been recognized as a TIME100 Most Influential Company and one of Fast Company’s Brands That Matter. Learn more at calm.com.

What We Do

At Calm we believe in making relaxation, better sleep, and mindfulness accessible to the entire world, and we hope you will help us achieve our mission. The Product & Design team is responsible for delivering Calm to our customers, ensuring that it is easy to use, supports their goals, and maintains a high level of quality across web, iOS, Android platforms.

As a Senior Product Designer on our Consumer team, you'll shape experiences used by tens of millions of people to sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully. People often reach for Calm in their most vulnerable moments, so the craft of what we make (how it looks, moves, and feels) matters enormously. 

This is a builder's role in the truest sense: you'll use AI and modern prototyping tools to move from insight to interactive prototype to shipped experience, not as a shortcut on quality, but to spend less time producing and more time on the judgment and detail that make an experience great. When anyone can generate a hundred screens in an afternoon, taste and judgment are the differentiators! 

The heart of this role is balancing velocity and craft in service of making our users healthier and happier, and building intuitive, engaging and impactful experiences that drive acquisition, engagement and retention.  You'll partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, Data Science, and Marketing, and set the standard for craft across iOS, Android, and web.  You will be a thought leader in design, helping to establish best practices and setting the bar for exceptional product design at Calm.

What You’ll Do

  • Own end-to-end product design initiatives that cover the whole product experience (visual, interaction, motion, brand integration), to create thoughtful, high-quality user-centered mobile experiences.
  • Prototype quickly in Figma and with AI and low-code tools like Replit, Lovable, and Claude, so you can get real, testable ideas in front of people early.
  • Present your design work clearly and persuasively to cross-functional stakeholders (including senior leadership), give and take feedback well, anchoring your rationale to both user needs and business goals.
  • Maintain strong attention to detail and collaboration through engineering implementation (build and QA) and post launch-iterations, to ensure high-quality execution.
  • Use data and drive research to inform the experiences you build, and leverage performance insights to evolve your approach.
  • Champion system-level thinking (improving how the team works and evolving Calm's design system) so the whole team works faster and smarter.
  • Balance multiple projects in a fast-paced environment while maintaining high standards of execution. 

Who You Are

  • Experienced Product Designer: 7+ years of experience in UX and UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile and web applications.
  • AI-native and tooling-fluent: Highly proficient in Figma for design, and already using AI and low-code tools (Replit, Lovable, Claude) to prototype and move fast, with the judgment to know when the output is good enough and when it isn't.
  • Technical agility: Comfortable shipping small code changes without engineering support, bridging the gap between design and engineering by personally shipping copy and UI polish directly.
  • A builder: Biased toward shipping and iterating over perfect plans. You'd rather put a working prototype in front of people than write a doc about one.
  • Data- and research-informed: You fold both qualitative and quantitative insight into your design decisions, and you measure whether the work landed.
  • A strong collaborator: A low-ego, trusted partner to Product, Research, and Engineering who makes the people around them better and helps sharpen how the team works.
  • High craft standards: A strong advocate for accessibility, consistency, visual storytelling, brand integration, and motion design to create engaging user experiences, while still maintaining velocity.
  • A clear communicator: You present your thinking persuasively to stakeholders and senior leadership, give and take feedback well, and champion an experience while staying open to being wrong.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with conversational or AI-native UX.
  • Experience working at multiple organizations, ideally including time at a consumer product in a fast-paced startup environment.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating your ability to design and ship beautiful, functional, and user-friendly experiences.
  • Comfort shipping small copy and UI changes directly in code, without engineering support.
  • A passion for Calm's mission and a point of view on how digital products can support mental health.

Minimum Requirements

  • 7+ years in UX/UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile (and web) applications.
  • Proven experience driving user testing and research.
  • Strong foundation in interaction design, visual design, and usability best practices.
  • Experience designing and shipping mobile applications at scale.
  • Hands-on proficiency in Figma and modern AI/prototyping tools.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing to a larger design vision and strategy.

jobs.title: AssemblyAI: Senior Research Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

Why AssemblyAI

AssemblyAI builds the best-in-class Voice AI models powering the next generation of voice applications. Our models serve 600M+ inference calls monthly, process 1M+ hours of audio daily, and power 2 billion+ end-user experiences. The Voice AI space is at an inflection point; we’re looking for folks truly excited to join a small team and help define the future of the industry.

We are one of the most capital-efficient AI companies on the planet - with under 100 people generating roughly $600K ARR per employee, we sit among the top 5 most revenue-dense teams within the fastest-growing AI companies today. That's not an accident; it's a deliberate choice to stay lean, move fast, and give every person on the team outsized ownership and impact. With thousands of customers including Granola, Fireflies, Figure AI, and CallRail, the company has real scale - processing over 2 million hours of audio daily and handling more than 1 million API calls every day. This is a rare growth-stage opportunity where the business is proven and the trajectory is steep, but the team is still small enough that your fingerprints are on everything.

If you've ever felt buried under layers of bureaucracy, starved of real ownership, or frustrated watching your work disappear into a slow-moving org, AssemblyAI is built differently. The company operates as a true meritocracy, with no heavy planning or approval processes and no gatekeeping on the tools or information you need. For anyone who genuinely cares about voice AI, not as a trend to chase, but as a technology to build,  this is the place where the most interesting problems at the most interesting scale are being solved by a team small enough that you'll actually know everyone's name.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. No matter your race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply!

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Research Engineer to join our Research team, developing and improving the systems behind large-scale distributed training, data processing, and inference. Our goal as an organization is to solve customer problems and improve our products quickly through model development and measurement — and how fast we move depends on how quickly anyone here can run an experiment, measure it, and find out what's wrong. Raising that ceiling is the heart of this role. You'll be working inside the pipeline you're improving, not alongside it.

The ideal candidate has a deep understanding of modern deep learning systems, combined with strong engineering expertise across JAX and TPUs, layer-level optimization, large-scale distributed training, streaming, low-latency and asynchronous inference, inference compilers, and advanced parallelization techniques.

This is a cross-functional role. You'll work closely with our researchers, our infrastructure team, and production engineering — not as a handoff point, but as the person who learns enough of each domain to follow problems through to resolution. At times you'll train models, run evaluations, and analyze data yourself, both to deliver impact directly and to learn what's worth building to multiply the team's work. The bar is someone who understands the end-to-end impact they intend to make, measures it from the outset, and would rather find out they were wrong in a week than in a quarter. That discipline is what turns cross-functional ownership into an advantage.

The role is embedded within the Research team. 

What You’ll Do

  • Raise the team's experimental velocity — make it faster to launch an experiment job, get a number back you can trust, and know what to try next.
  • Maintain and evolve our JAX training framework, keeping it scalable and efficient for large-scale distributed training runs on TPU.
  • Improve the data our models learn from: investigating quality issues, building the tooling to surface them, and turning what you find into measurable accuracy gains.
  • Analyze the accuracy of production models, build evaluation harnesses, and work out which improvements will matter most to customers.
  • Translate research prototypes into production-ready systems, refactoring and modernizing model architectures and infrastructure along the way.
  • Optimize production inference for speech language models, both from a serving architecture perspective and through advanced techniques such as quantization and speculative decoding.
  • Investigate and resolve performance bottlenecks across the stack, from low-level kernels (XLA, Pallas) to high-level system design.
  • Partner with researchers, infrastructure, and production engineering to trace problems to their real source and ship fixes that hold.

What You’ll Need

  • Expert-level proficiency with JAX and TPUs, including the surrounding ecosystem (Flax, Optax, the XLA compilation pipeline).
  • Measurement discipline. You define what success looks like before you start, you stay skeptical of your own results until they hold up, and you treat an unexplained improvement as a problem rather than a win.
  • Appetite for the whole pipeline. Your core strength might be JAX and TPU performance, but when a customer issue traces back to a data problem or an evaluation blind spot, you want to go find it yourself. The people who do well here went deep in one area first, then kept expanding outward.
  • Strong experience optimizing inference systems for production, ideally with LLMs or speech models.
  • Deep understanding of distributed training at scale, modern deep learning systems, and ML infrastructure best practices.
  • Familiarity with modern inference optimization techniques: continuous batching, KV-cache management, sharding strategies, quantization.
  • Enthusiasm for refactoring and improving existing systems — you thrive on making products and code faster and better.
  • Strong Python skills; C++ or Rust experience for kernel-level work is a plus.
  • Excellent communication and a collaborative mindset — you can clearly explain complex tradeoffs and prioritize high-impact work.

Bonus

  • Domain knowledge in Speech-to-Text: ASR architectures, audio processing, streaming inference.

jobs.title: Stripe: Abuse Research Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote from the US

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence.  Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains.  Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

Responsibilities

  • Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.
  • FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints.  
  • Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows.  
  • Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security.  
  • Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls.  

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains.  
  • 5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems.  
  • B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.  
  • Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines.  
  • Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation methodologies.  
  • Strong communication skills with a proven ability to translate complex technical research into clear, actionable recommendations and advisories for cross-functional partners.

Preferred qualifications

  • Deep technical understanding of threat actor motivations, infrastructure, and TTPs specific to financial fraud (e.g., ATO, Card Testing, Credential Stuffing). 
  • Familiarity with standardized taxonomies such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&CK.  
  • Proficiency with engineering, data processing, and analysis platforms such as Databricks, Trino, PySpark, Pandas, or Scikit-Learn.  
  • Proven background utilizing Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs), tactical threat feeds, OSINT, and breach intelligence. 
  • Demonstrated capability building or leveraging agentic LLM tools, automated testing systems, or control validation frameworks to model adversary behavior at scale.  
  • Participation in industry conferences, webinars, or threat-sharing groups, alongside relevant professional certifications (e.g., GCTI, GCFA, OSCP).

About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

As the Senior Staff Machine Learning Platform Engineer, you will own the technical vision and evolution of Faire’s ML platform. You will set standards, influence org-wide architecture, and lead complex, cross-functional initiatives that unlock data science velocity at scale.  This role will also be key to adapting ML workflows to take advantage of modern AI productivity tools.   • Lead adoption and advanced use of Unity Catalog, multi-workspace strategies, and data/ML mesh patterns
  • Architect highly scalable ML workflows using Spark, Delta Lake, and MLflow
  • Optimize performance, reliability, and cost of the ML platform
  • Evaluate and integrate emerging Databricks features
  • Stay ahead of the curve by engaging with the latest developments in machine learning and AI
  • Serve as senior ML technical advisor to Faire’s data science and production engineering teams 
  • Represent Faire at ML conferences and meetups
  • Mentor ML engineers and raise the overall bar for Machine Learning at Faire

  • 10-12 years of experience building and improving large-scale ML or data platforms.
  • A degree (preferably graduate level) in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, or a related technical field.
  • Deep expertise in Databricks lakehouse architecture, including governance via Unity catalog, orchestration via Workflows, and cost optimization
  • Proven ability to design systems that support multiple data science teams and production workloads
  • Strong background in distributed systems, ML infrastructure, and cloud architecture.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership across teams and orgs; ability to influence without authority
  • Experience integrating LLM workflows into enterprise platforms is a plus
  • Previous contributions to open source ML Infrastructure projects or research publications is a very strong plus

Faire uses a modern cloud based tech stack.  For this role, you’ll want to be proficient with the following:

Category

Technologies

Languages

Python, SQL, Kotlin

ML Frameworks

PyTorch, PySpark, MLFlow 

Big Data & Processing

Spark, Kafka, Databricks, Snowflake, Fivetran, Iceberg, Unity Catalog, Datadog, Airflow, Cockroach DB, MySQL

Cloud & Infrastructure

AWS, S3, SageMaker, Kubernetes, Docker, GitHub Actions, Terraform

Generative AI

Claude Sonnet 4.5, ChatGPT 5.2

Canada: the pay range for this role is $248,000 to $341,000 per year. 

This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday). Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting. 

Why you’ll love working at Faire

  • Move fast: You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.
  • Equipped to scale: We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.
  • Best in class: Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.
  • Real rewards. Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.
  • Belonging: We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.

Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. At Counterpart Health (CPH), we are transforming healthcare and improving patient care with our innovative primary care tool, Counterpart Assistant (CA). By supporting Primary Care Physicians (PCPs), we are able to deliver improved outcomes to patients at a lower cost through early diagnosis and longitudinal care management of chronic conditions.

We're seeking a Commercial Partnerships & Operations Director to shape and drive key commercial initiatives and strategic partnerships. Reporting to the VP of Commercial Innovations & Partnerships, you'll partner closely with CPH leadership, owning a portfolio of high-impact initiatives and external partnerships.

This role is a senior individual contributor who is a highly organized, analytical, and execution-focused operator who can move fluidly between the details of execution and the strategic context, bringing forward recommendations and insights that shape leadership decisions. You'll lead cross-functional programs, keep priorities on track, align stakeholders, manage external relationships, and deliver the insights and materials needed to support strategic decisions and accelerate Counterpart Health's growth and execution capabilities.

As a Commercial Partnerships & Operations Director, you will:

  • Lead high-priority commercial initiatives: Own the execution of high priority cross-functional programs by defining project plans, tracking milestones, mitigating risks, resolving dependencies, and ensuring timely delivery of strategic outcomes.
  • Drive cross-functional execution: Lead efforts across Commercial, Product, Engineering, Clinical, Operations, Legal, and external partners to align stakeholders, maintain momentum, and deliver on commitments.
  • Manage strategic partnerships: Own key external partnerships by establishing governance, aligning strategic objectives, driving executive engagement, resolving risks, and ensuring successful execution throughout the partnership lifecycle.
  • Deliver business insights: Develop and lead analytical models, dashboards, and performance trackers to monitor results, generate insights, and inform commercial decision-making.
  • Prepare executive communications: Develop executive-level presentations, reports, and recommendations that frame strategic options, clarify tradeoffs, and guide decisions by leadership and external partners.
  • Strengthen program execution: Translate enterprise commercial priorities into actionable plans with defined owners, timelines, deliverables, and accountability while proactively identifying and resolving execution risks.
  • Enhance operational effectiveness: Design and implement scalable processes, tools, templates, and reporting mechanisms that improve coordination, visibility, and execution across the Commercial Innovations & Partnerships team.
  • Serve as a trusted operator: Serve as a trusted commercial advisor by anticipating enterprise risks, challenging assumptions, recommending solutions, and maintaining alignment across multiple high-stakes initiatives.

Success in this Role Looks Like:

  • In the first 90 days: Build a strong understanding of CPH's commercial strategy, products, partnerships, and operating model. Establish relationships across internal teams and external partners. Take ownership of key initiatives and establish greater strategic clarity, accountability, visibility, and execution discipline.
  • In the first 6 months: Independently own a portfolio of commercial initiatives and strategic partnership workstreams. Implement effective project management processes and reporting frameworks.Deliver high-quality analyses and recommendations that influence executive decision-making and drive progress.
  • At the end of your first year: Become a trusted execution partner to the VP of Commercial Innovations & Partnerships and the CPH leadership team. Successfully lead multiple complex initiatives from planning through execution.Strengthen partnership performance, enhance cross-functional execution, and scale the Commercial Innovations & Partnerships function.

You should get in touch if:

  • 6–10 years of experience in healthcare consulting, a healthcare technology company, or a similar execution-focused role in a high-growth healthcare organization.

  • Proven ability to manage complex, cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities; experience in a Project Management Office (PMO) or dedicated program management role is a plus.
  • Exceptional organizational and project management skills, with a track record of bringing structure, accountability, and execution to complex initiatives.

  • Strong analytical skills with advanced proficiency in AI tools, Excel, and Google Sheets, including experience building financial models, dashboards, trackers, and other reporting tools.
  • Excellent written and visual communication skills, with the ability to create executive-ready presentations and synthesize complex information into clear, actionable insights.
  • Strong knowledge of Medicare and Medicare Advantage, value-based care, healthcare operations, and payer-provider dynamics.
  • Ability to thrive in fast-paced environments, manage multiple priorities, and adapt to changing business needs while maintaining a high standard of quality.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive results through strong organization, collaboration, communication, and execution rather than formal authority.

Benefits Overview: 

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.
